content:
jamie: FYI ran the rampdown sims against last week's ECC burst data. posting results and proposed threshold tweaks.
ops-bot: Alert: ECC spike on pool-gpu-3 at 2025-11-02T09:03:21Z (count++).
jamie: TL;DR — current policy (`threshold=30/min, window=60s, consecutive=1`) triggers too eagerly on noisy cards. we saw 18x false evacuations in sim.
ravi: Can you share the sim assumptions? traffic distribution, seq lengths, mix of models?
jamie: Yep — 72h trace sampled from prod serving (mixed LLMs), sequence dist heavy tail, 70% <128 tokens. we injected ECC bursts matching last month's peaks and ran 10k trials.
sofia: rough numbers? capacity impact?
jamie: Summary: with current policy capacity loss ~12% under median burst, P95 loss 28%. False-positive (single transient spike) eviction rate 0.9% -> approx 800 cards/month.
marco: Oof. cost and availability hit. What about hysteresis or multi-window checks?
jamie: Exactly what I experimented with. Two candidate policies:

```
policy A: threshold=50/min, window=120s, consecutive=2, soft-evict=true, requeue-delay=10m
policy B: threshold=30/min, window=60s, consecutive=3, soft-evict=false, immediate-evac=true
```

jamie: Sim results: A -> capacity loss median 3%, P95 7%, false-evict 0.07%. B -> capacity loss median 5%, P95 12%, false-evict 0.15%.
ravi: soft-evict makes a big diff. how do we define soft-evict?
jamie: Soft-evict = move workloads off-card but keep card in pool for lower-priority batch jobs; don't mark as unhealthy for replacement. Hard-evict = drain + mark for replacement/repair.
sofia: Can we combine with routing fallback to cheaper model variants instead of draining? e.g., route to fp16-quant or smaller model while keeping card in warm standby.
jamie: Yes — the sim included a fallback policy that reroutes 30% of requests to lower-cost variant when a soft-evict is in effect. that reduced tail latency impact by ~40% and regained capacity headroom.
marco: Any telemetry additions needed to reduce FP further? maybe card-level SNR or ECC pattern classification?
jamie: We added a simple enrichment: require `ecc_type` to be one of {multi-bit, persistent-xid} OR if single-bit, require repeated across two windows. That cut FPs in half.
sofia: Nice. What about regional constraints? eu-west pools are smaller, will soft-evict cause cross-region spill?
jie: (typo) I mean jamie: For eu-west we saw more severe impact because pools are smaller. Proposed: use policy A globally but tighten for small pools: for pool size <50 GPUs use `threshold=60/min` or increase consecutive to 3.
marco: Sounds pragmatic. Any automation risk of oscillation (drain/un-drain loops)?
jamie: We added backoff: once soft-evicted, card won't be considered for re-add for 15m; if reinstated, require stable window 30m. reduces flip-flopping.
sofia: Ops runbook section? can we outline manual override steps?
jamie: Draft runbook: 1) Alert fires -> automated soft-evict if policy A conditions met. 2) Post to #eng-oncall with summary and suggested action. 3) If card shows repeated hard ECC (multi-bit/persistent-xid) in 2h -> schedule replacement and mark out of rotation. 4) If false positive suspected -> undo soft-evict via `gpuctl unsoft-evict <card>` and annotate event.
ravi: Can you paste the minimal config snippet to ship to fleet agent?
jamie: Sure:

```
fleet_policy:
  name: ecc_dynamic_v2
  soft_evict: true
  threshold_per_min: 50
  window_seconds: 120
  consecutive_windows: 2
  requeue_delay_minutes: 10
  backoff_minutes: 15
  small_pool_adjustment:
    min_size: 50
    threshold_per_min: 60
```

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: infra/fleet-policies@ecc-dynamic-v2 commit: d4f8a1a -> staging (link: https://git.internal/revision/d4f8a1a) :rocket:
marco: Can we run a canary rollout to eu-west pool-2 for 24h and run chaos tests?
jamie: Yes — plan: canary 5% capacity in eu-west pool-2 for 24h, enable extra logging, and run synthetic ECC injection at 2x usual rate.
sofia: Who owns the canary?
jamie: Assigned to @ravi to coordinate with @oncall (we'll ping ops).
ravi: I can own. I'll schedule injection, monitor telemetry, and have rollback ready.
sofia: Add postmortem template if we hit >1 hard-evac in canary.
jamie: Will add.
marco: Final question — what's the expected reduction in false replacements by moving to policy A?
jamie: From 800/month -> ~60/month across fleet in sims. big win for both cost and repair churn.
sofia: SGTM. Next steps?
jamie: 1) push infra change to staging (done, see deploy link). 2) canary in eu-west (ravi). 3) collect 24h metrics and decide global rollout. 4) add SNR + ecc_type enrichment to telemetry pipeline (sofia + infra-telemetry).
ops-bot: Note: created incident-ops ticket #INC-2025-214 for canary monitoring.
ravi: I'll post status updates in this thread during canary.
marco: Thanks all. cc @hardware-team for replacement policy alignment.
sofia: :thumbsup:
